info.text: Four questions on this topic. Unlimited attempts, immediate feedback, zero weight.

name.text: T1Q1 Short description of what is tested

questiontext.text:
Five students sat a station and scored 78, 70, 91, 55 and 83.

scores <- c(78, 70, 91, 55, 83)

sum(scores >= 70)

What does the second line print?

generalfeedback.text: 4. The comparison gives one TRUE or FALSE per student, and sum() counts each TRUE as 1. The bar matters: >= keeps the student who scored exactly 70, > drops them. Whenever a threshold is "70 or above" or "under 5", that single character decides whether a real person is counted.

feedback.text: That is the answer to sum(scores > 70), which drops the student who scored exactly 70. >= means greater than or equal to, so that student is counted and the answer is 4.
That is how many students there are, which is length(scores). Only four of them reached 70. The student who scored 55 did not.
That is the total of the five marks, sum(scores). Here sum() is being given the comparison, not the marks, so it adds up TRUEs rather than scores.
